subject.title: Feature: configPatch in plugin manifest — automatic config setup on install

question: Which bounded shared-config operations may external plugins request at install time, and what consent, conflict, provenance, rollback, uninstall, and noninteractive policies are required?
rationale: The capability is genuinely missing, but implementing it grants third-party package metadata new authority over persisted user policy; source mechanics cannot safely choose that trust boundary.

options.title: Transactional bounded intents
options.body: Add typed approved operations to canonical setup metadata and apply them atomically with install records after required diff review and consent.

options.title: Owner-specific setup only
options.body: Keep installation limited to enablement and records, with shared configuration performed by provider, channel, or plugin-specific setup flows.

options.title: Raw automatic patch
options.body: Deep-merge arbitrary manifest objects into shared configuration during plugin installation.

recommendation.title: Transactional bounded intents
recommendation.body: Add typed approved operations to canonical setup metadata and apply them atomically with install records after required diff review and consent.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the dominant current-history owner and authored the latest review of this exact setup and trust-boundary question.
